I'm sketching out sample grids with lines and dots, testing color pairings for horizontal and vertical lines, but realizing overlapping lines at the same row/column create conflicts, so I'll stick to one line type per grid to keep things consistent.

For grid 1 I'll use a horizontal line with dots that shift to the adjacent row; grid 2 uses a vertical line with dots shifting a column over; grid 3 pairs a larger canvas with a horizontal line and multiple dots shifting to the row above it. I need to make sure stray colors placed elsewhere don't accidentally form their own uniform rows or columns, and that dots aren't placed directly on the line's row or column.
